mainTopic: Does an accepted oath free a שומר from paying when witnesses later show he lied, and how far does רב's rule reach?
overview: The גמרא finishes a discussion of רב ששת's view that a שומר who denies holding a פקדון becomes a גזלן right away. It answers a challenge from אילפא's words 'שבועה קונה' in two ways. One answer is that אילפא means an animal standing in an אגם. The other is that he means רב הונא's ruling in the name of רב: once the owner accepts a שבועה, the one who swore no longer pays, even if witnesses come later. The גמרא then examines that ruling. רבא first suggests it fits only a loan, but then agrees it covers a deposit too. רב נחמן defends רב against a משנה by distinguishing an oath taken outside court and an oath the שומר 'jumped' into. רב המנונא and רבא bring more challenges. רבא finally limits רב's rule to a שומר who claimed the item was lost, swore, never admitted, and was exposed by witnesses. רב אשי questions this limitation, and רב אחא סבא begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Denying a deposit makes one unfit to testify
steps.stepSummary: The end of a quoted ruling: someone who falsely denies holding a פקדון is פסול לעדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one who denies a deposit is disqualified from testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that began just before this section. Someone who denies holding a פקדון is treated as a liar and cannot be a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Denying a loan can be an honest delay, since the borrower already spent the money. But a פקדון sits in the שומר's hands, so denying it is an outright lie, a kind of theft. This fits רב ששת's idea that כפירה in a פקדון turns the שומר into a גזלן.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit, an object left with someone to guard
Disqualified from serving as a witness

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The first half, about denying a loan, came right before this section.

phrases.english: [One who denies] a deposit is disqualified from testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling quoted before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who falsely denies holding a פקדון is פסול לעדות.

steps.title: Challenge from אילפא: only an oath makes it his
steps.stepSummary: אילפא said 'שבועה קונה', which implies that כפירה alone does not make the שומר the owner. That seems to contradict רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't אילפא say, 'An oath acquires'? This implies an oath acquires, but a denial does not acquire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. אילפא's wording suggests that only a שבועה makes the item belong to the שומר, so a denial alone should not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת says the moment the שומר denies, he is a גזלן and liable for אונסין. אילפא singles out the oath as the point of acquisition. From his words the גמרא infers that a mere כפירה does not acquire, which goes against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath acquires: the item becomes his, so he is responsible like a thief
Denial of a claim
Acquires (Aramaic)

phrases.english: But didn't אילפא say:
An oath acquires.
[This implies] it is an oath that acquires,
but a denial does not acquire!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty against רב ששת's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that כפירה alone makes the שומר a גזלן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אילפא's words imply that only a שבועה acquires, so a denial without an oath should not.

steps.title: אילפא speaks of an animal in a swamp
steps.stepSummary: אילפא's case is one where the deposit is out in an אגם, not in the שומר's hands. There a denial alone does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where it stands in a swamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אילפא is talking about a deposit that is out in a swamp, not under the שומר's control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the item is not in his possession, a denial may just be a way to put the owner off, so it does not make it his. Only an oath does. When the item is in his house, a denial alone acquires, just as רב ששת said.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: the same answer used earlier applies here
Swamp or marsh, a place outside the שומר's control

phrases.english: Here too, it is where [the animal] stands in a swamp.
phrases.notes: 'Here too' means the same swamp answer the גמרא already used just before this section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from אילפא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אילפא means that a denial never acquires, which goes against רב ששת.
steps.terutzMaskana: אילפא's case is a deposit out in an אגם. When the item is in the שומר's possession, a denial alone acquires.

steps.title: Second answer: 'acquires' means he no longer pays
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, 'שבועה קונה' follows רב הונא in the name of רב. After the owner accepts a שבועה, the one who swore is פטור from paying, even if witnesses later show he lied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: what does 'an oath acquires' mean? It follows רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: if one says 'I have a מנה in your hand' and the other says 'You have nothing in my hand,' and he swears, and later witnesses come, he is exempt. The פסוק says 'and its owner shall accept, and he shall not pay.' Once the owner accepted an oath, he no longer pays money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. אילפא was not speaking about when a שומר becomes a גזלן at all. He meant that after a שבועה, the money claim is closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'acquires' means the oath ends the owner's right to collect, based on the פסוק in שמות. So אילפא's statement has nothing to do with liability for אונסין, and it does not clash with רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces a second, alternative answer
A sum of money (one hundred זוז)
And the other one
Exempt
And its owner shall accept, and he shall not pay

steps.confusionAlert: 'Acquires' here does not mean he becomes a thief who is liable for accidents. It means the oath closes the claim, so he does not pay even if witnesses later come.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רב הונא's ruling, which the גמרא now goes on to examine on its own.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What is [meant by] 'an oath acquires'?
It is like [the ruling of] רב הונא,
as רב הונא said that רב said:
[If one says] 'I have a מנה in your hand,'
and the other says: 'You have nothing in my hand,'

phrases.aramaic: וְנִשְׁבַּע, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: and he swore, and afterward witnesses came, he is exempt,
as it is said: 'And its owner shall accept, and he shall not pay.'
Once the owner has accepted an oath,
he no longer pays money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in step 2, as an alternative to step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שבועה קונה' is about when the שומר becomes a גזלן liable for אונסין.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שבועה קונה' means that after the owner accepts a שבועה, the one who swore never has to pay, so it does not clash with רב ששת.

steps.title: רב הונא's ruling stated on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to discuss רב הונא's ruling by itself: once the owner accepts an oath, the one who swore is exempt, even if witnesses come later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב הונא said that רב said: if one says 'I have a מנה in your hand' and the other says 'You have nothing at all in my hand,' and he swears, and witnesses come, he is exempt. The פסוק says 'and its owner shall accept, and he shall not pay.' Once the owner accepted an oath, they no longer pay money.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא turns to examine רב הונא's ruling in its own right. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is repeated here not to answer רב ששת, but as the starting point for a new discussion about it. The rule is that a שבועה the owner accepted closes the money claim, based on the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא returns to look at a statement it just quoted
Money

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read 'שבועה קונה'. Either it is about a deposit in an אגם, or it is רב הונא's rule that an accepted oath ends the duty to pay. רב הונא's rule is now about to be examined.

phrases.english: The matter itself.
רב הונא said that רב said:
[If one says] 'I have a מנה in your hand,'
and the other says: 'You have nothing at all in my hand,'
and he swore, and witnesses came, he is exempt,
as it is said: 'And its owner shall accept, and he shall not pay.'
Once the owner has accepted an oath,
they no longer pay money.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ruling quoted in step 4 and opens a new discussion about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the owner accepts a שבועה, the one who swore is פטור from paying, even if witnesses later prove he lied.

steps.title: רבא suggests רב's rule fits only a loan
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it makes sense that רב's rule applies to a מלוה, because loan money is given in order to be spent. A פקדון is different, because it stays in the owner's possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב's ruling makes sense for a loan, since a loan is given to be spent. But a deposit stays in the owner's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a reason to limit רב's rule from step 4 to loans only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loan money is supposed to be used up, so the borrower really owes money, and the Torah can free him through an oath. A deposit still belongs to the owner wherever it is. So, on this reasoning, an oath should not take it away from him.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan
It was given to be spent
It stays in its owner's possession

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rav's statement makes sense with a loan,
phrases.notes: This is the rule רב הונא said in the name of רב in step 5: after an accepted oath, the one who swore is exempt.

phrases.english: which is given to be spent;
but a deposit stays in its owner's possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes limiting the scope of רב הונא's ruling from step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Possibly, רב's exemption after an oath applies only to a loan, not to a deposit.

steps.title: רבא retracts: רב meant it even for a deposit
steps.stepSummary: רבא swears that רב said his rule even about a פקדון, because the פסוק that gives the exemption is written about a deposit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by God, רב said it even about a deposit, because the verse itself is written about a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes back the limit he just suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source of the exemption is a פסוק that speaks about a deposit. So the rule cannot leave deposits out. The reasoning from step 6 gives way to the plain reading of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: By God (a strong oath-like way of saying 'I am certain')
The פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Final position: רב's rule (an accepted oath exempts from paying) applies to a פקדון too.

phrases.english: But, by God, Rav said it even about a deposit;
for when the verse is written, it is written about a deposit.
phrases.notes: שמות 22:10, "ולקח בעליו ולא ישלם", which is said about a שומר holding someone's item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limit proposed in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רב's rule is limited to loans
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The very פסוק behind the exemption speaks about a deposit

steps.title: Challenge from a משנה where a lying bailee still pays
steps.stepSummary: While רב נחמן teaches רב's rule, רב אחא בר מניומי challenges him from a משנה. A שומר who swore that the deposit was lost, and witnesses then show he used it, must pay the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן was teaching this rule. רב אחא בר מניומי challenged him: If the owner asks 'Where is my deposit?' and the bailee says 'It is lost,' and the owner says 'I make you swear' and he answers 'Amen,' and witnesses then testify that he ate it, he pays the principal. If he admits on his own, he pays the principal, a fifth, and brings an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב נחמן teaching the rule. Then a משנה is brought that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the owner accepted the שומר's oath, and witnesses still make him pay the קרן. That goes against רב's rule that an accepted oath frees him from paying even if witnesses come later.

keyTerms.meaning: I make you swear
The principal (the item's basic value)
The extra fifth paid by one who admits a false oath
Guilt-offering

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב נַחְמָן וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman was sitting and saying this teaching.
phrases.notes: "This teaching" is רב's rule that an accepted oath exempts, even if witnesses come later.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Minyumi challenged Rav Nachman:
"Where is my deposit?" He said to him: "It is lost."
"I make you swear," and he said: "Amen,"
and the witnesses testify about him that he ate it —
phrases.notes: "Ate it" just means he used the item up for himself.

phrases.english: he pays the principal.
If he admitted on his own —
he pays principal and a fifth and brings a guilt-offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the now-established rule (it applies even to a deposit) against a משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that an accepted oath exempts from payment even if witnesses later contradict it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has a bailee who swore with the owner's acceptance, yet witnesses still obligate him to pay the קרן

steps.title: רב נחמן: the משנה's oath was outside of court
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה speaks of an oath taken outside בית דין. Such an oath does not bring the exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: What case are we dealing with? One where he swore outside of court.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends the rule by placing the משנה in a special setting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a proper oath in court frees the שומר from paying. An oath outside court does not count for that, so the witnesses can still make him pay.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here?
Outside of court

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he swore outside of court.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן כְּגוֹן דְּנִשְׁבַּע חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the source (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's oath is an ordinary oath that should exempt
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's oath was outside court, so it never brought an exemption

steps.title: The משנה's last part speaks of double payment
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא answers back from the סיפא. A שומר who swore the item was stolen, and is then shown to have stolen it, pays כפל. כפל only applies to an oath in court, so the משנה cannot be about an oath outside court.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: If so, look at the last part: 'Where is my deposit?' 'It was stolen.' 'I make you swear.' 'Amen.' Witnesses show he stole it, so he pays double. If he admits on his own, he pays principal, a fifth, and an אשם. If you think this is outside of court, would there be double payment?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא pushes back against רב נחמן's answer by using the second half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Double payment for a שומר who falsely claims theft comes only from an oath in court. Since the סיפא gives כפל, it must be talking about an oath in court. That suggests the רישא is also in court, so רב נחמן's answer seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part of the source
It was stolen
Double payment
And if you think

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא:
phrases.english: He said to him: If so, say the last part:
"Where is my deposit?" He said to him: "It was stolen."
"I make you swear," and he said: "Amen,"
and the witnesses testify about him that he stole it —
he pays double payment.
If he admitted on his own —
he pays principal and a fifth and brings a guilt-offering.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין,
phrases.english: And if you think it is outside of court,
is there double payment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the משנה deals with an oath outside court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא gives כפל, which only happens with an oath in court, so the משנה must be about an oath in court

steps.title: רב נחמן could split the משנה but refuses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says he could answer that the רישא is outside court and the סיפא is in court. He will not give such a forced answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I could answer you that the first part is outside of court and the last part is in court. But I will not give you a forced answer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן mentions a possible answer and then sets it aside. This prepares his real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting two parts of one משנה that sound exactly alike into two different settings would be a strained reading. So רב נחמן looks for an answer that keeps both parts in court.

keyTerms.meaning: I am able to answer you
The first part of the source
A forced, strained answer

steps.confusionAlert: The split answer (רישא outside court, סיפא in court) is NOT רב נחמן's real answer. He only mentions it to reject it.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am able to answer you:
the first part is outside of court,
and the last part is in court;

phrases.aramaic: מִיהוּ שִׁינּוּיָא דְּחִיקָא לָא מְשַׁנֵּינָא לָךְ.
phrases.english: but I will not answer you with a forced answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and then sets aside one possible answer to step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source (רישא and סיפא in different settings), which he then declines
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each part of the משנה could have its own setting
steps.terutzMaskana: That answer is too forced to use

steps.title: Both parts are in court: he 'jumped' to swear or he did not
steps.stepSummary: Both the רישא and the סיפא are oaths in court. In the רישא the שומר jumped in and swore before the court required it, so his oath does not exempt him. In the סיפא he swore properly when the court required it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both parts are in court, and there is no difficulty. Here he jumped ahead and swore, and there he did not jump.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his real answer, which keeps the whole משנה in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath the שומר rushes into before בית דין asks for it is not a full oath, so it does not free him from paying, and he pays the קרן. An oath imposed by the court is a full oath, so it brings כפל in the סיפא. רב's rule survives, because it only applies to a proper court oath.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, both
He jumped, meaning he swore before the court told him to

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule (an accepted oath exempts from paying even if witnesses come later) applies only to a proper oath required by בית דין. If the שומר 'jumped' and swore on his own, he still pays.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the condition for the exemption: only a real court-imposed oath counts. This keeps רב's rule in line with the משנה.

phrases.english: Both this and that are in court —
and it is not difficult;
here, where he jumped,
phrases.notes: He rushed to swear right after the claim, before the court ever required an oath from him.

phrases.english: there, where he did not jump.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּבֵית דִּין וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the preferred answer to the קשיא of step 10, in place of the forced answer of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two cases within the same setting (כאן וכאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both parts of the משנה describe the same kind of court oath, so they contradict רב
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is an oath the שומר jumped into (no exemption, so he pays the קרן). The סיפא is a court-required oath (a full oath, so כפל applies).

steps.title: Why defend רב if you disagree with him?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב נחמן why he defended רב's rule against the challenges, since רב נחמן himself does not hold like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said to רב נחמן: You don't even agree with רב. So why do you put yourself on the line to defend him?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the back-and-forth with רב אחא is over, רמי בר חמא asks רב נחמן a personal question: why did he defend a view he does not hold?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 9-12, רב נחמן answered every challenge to רב's rule. But it is known that רב נחמן himself does not agree with רב. So רמי בר חמא wants to know why he bothered.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / after all (opens a point both sides already accept)
You do not hold this view
Literally 'pledging yourself': putting yourself on the line to defend someone

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said to Rav Naḥman:
After all, you do not hold like Rav,
so why do you pledge yourself on behalf of Rav?
phrases.notes: He means: why work so hard to protect רב's rule from the questions?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the defense that רב נחמן gave in steps 9-12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רב נחמן defend רב, if he does not agree with רב's rule?

steps.title: רב נחמן was only explaining רב's view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he was not ruling like רב. He was only showing how רב himself would explain the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did it to explain רב's view, because this is how רב would explain our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains that his answers were meant to show how רב reads the משנה. They were not his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can explain how someone else's view fits the sources without agreeing with that view. רב נחמן was only showing that רב's rule does not clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: To explain it
Explains or settles (a difficulty in a text)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: an אמורא may defend a view only to explain it, without ruling that way.

phrases.english: He said to him: To explain the view of Rav,
since this is how Rav would explain our mishna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was only showing how רב would read the משנה. He was not accepting רב's ruling.

steps.title: But רב based his rule on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן can disagree with רב, since רב took his rule straight from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב quoted a פסוק! How can you argue with that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's choice to disagree with רב. רב's rule seemed to come from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב learned his rule from ״וְלָקַח בְּעָלָיו וְלֹא יְשַׁלֵּם״. He read it to mean that once the owner accepts the oath, no payment is due. If the rule comes from the תורה, how can רב נחמן reject it?

keyTerms.meaning: But look (opens a challenge)
A פסוק

phrases.english: But Rav quoted a verse!
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק רב used earlier: ״וְלָקַח בְּעָלָיו וְלֹא יְשַׁלֵּם״ (שמות 22:10).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's position from step 14, where he admitted he does not hold like רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's rule has a source in a פסוק, so it seems no one can disagree with it.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches who swears
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק teaches a different rule. Whenever the תורה requires an oath, the one who would have to pay is the one who swears, and he does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: The פסוק comes to teach that all who swear in the תורה swear and do not pay. ״And the owner shall accept it, and he shall not pay″ means the one who would have to pay is the one who swears.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the פסוק is teaching something else, so it is not a proof for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב read the פסוק as: after the oath, the שומר is exempt even if witnesses come later. Those who disagree read it as only telling us who takes the oath: the person being asked to pay, not the person asking for money. With that reading, the פסוק says nothing about witnesses who come after the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: The people the תורה requires to take an oath
They swear and do not pay
The one who would have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the same פסוק. The argument is only about what the פסוק teaches: רב says it exempts the שומר after the oath, and the other reading says it only tells us who swears.

phrases.english: They said: The verse comes for 'All who take oaths in the Torah'
'take oaths and do not pay.'
'And the owner shall accept it, and he shall not pay' means:
the one who would have to pay is the one who swears.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: קְרָא לְ״כׇל הַנִּשְׁבָּעִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה – נִשְׁבָּעִין וְלֹא מְשַׁלְּמִין״ הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by giving the פסוק a different meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק teaches רב's rule: after an oath in court, the שומר is exempt even if witnesses come later.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only teaches that the one who would pay is the one who swears, and that his oath frees him from paying. It is not a proof for רב's rule.

steps.title: רב המנונא's challenge: liable for every one of five oaths
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא challenges רב from a משנה. A person was made to swear five times, in court or outside court, and denied each time. He is liable for every single oath, because he could always go back and admit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected: If the owner made him swear five times, in court or outside court, and he denied each time, he is liable for each one. רבי שמעון said: What is the reason? Because he can always go back and admit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רב's rule begins. רב המנונא quotes a משנה about someone who swore falsely five times about a deposit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says each oath makes him liable. That only works if, after each oath, he still owes the money and could still admit and pay. But רב says that once a person swears in court he is exempt. If so, after the first oath he owes nothing, so the later oaths would deny nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He made him swear about it
Denied (the claim)
To go back and admit

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raised an objection:
If he made him swear about it five times,
phrases.notes: This is the owner making the one holding his deposit swear about it.

phrases.english: whether in front of the court
or not in front of the court,

phrases.aramaic: וְכָפַר עָלָיו – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: and he denied it, he is liable for each and every one.
And Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason?
Since he is able to go back and admit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new attack on רב's rule from a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that an oath in court exempts the שומר even if witnesses come later
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being liable for every oath means he still owes money after each oath. That goes against רב, who says the oath in court ends the duty to pay.

steps.title: The earlier escape answers do not work here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the earlier answers cannot save רב here. The משנה says the owner made him swear, so he did not jump in. It also says 'in front of the court', so it is not only about an oath outside court.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, you cannot say he jumped in, because it says 'he made him swear'. You cannot say it was outside court, because it says 'in front of the court'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes רב המנונא's challenge stronger. It shows that the two answers that worked for the earlier משנה do not work for this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 רב נחמן answered with 'outside court', and in step 12 with 'he jumped in'. Here the wording 'he made him swear' rules out jumping in. The words 'in front of the court' rule out the claim that the oath was only outside court.

keyTerms.meaning: Jumped in (swore before the court asked him to)
You cannot say
It teaches (the wording of the source says)
Outside court

steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא's משנה closes both escape answers: the oath was required ('he made him swear') and it was taken in court. So it seems to be a direct challenge to רב.

phrases.english: And here, you cannot say he jumped in,
phrases.notes: This refers to the answer in step 12, where the שומר swore before the court required it.

phrases.english: since it teaches 'he made him swear about it';

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ –
phrases.english: you cannot say it was outside court,
since it teaches 'in front of the court'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 17 by ruling out the answers from steps 9 and 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: Possible ways to defend רב using the 'jumped in' or 'outside court' answers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording of the משנה ('he made him swear', 'in front of the court') rules out both answers.

steps.title: The same רב המנונא answers his own challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא, who asked the question, also answers it. The משנה is talking about two different cases: 'he made him swear' is outside court, and 'in court' is where the שומר jumped in to swear on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked it and he answered it. The משנה is talking about separate cases. 'The owner made him swear' happened outside court. 'In court' is a case where the שומר jumped in and swore on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רב המנונא himself answered his question. He split the משנה into two separate cases, so neither one is the case רב was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the problem was that the משנה seemed to have both 'the owner made him swear' and 'in court' in one case. רב המנונא now says these are two different cases: being made to swear happened outside court, and the oath in court happened when the שומר jumped in. So the משנה never talks about a שומר who was made to swear in court, and that is exactly where רב's rule applies.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He asked the question and he answered it himself
It is teaching separate cases, not one combined case
He jumped in, meaning he swore on his own without being asked
He made him swear

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as one story where he was made to swear in court. The answer is that 'made to swear' and 'in court' belong to two different cases.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ, וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ;
phrases.english: He raised the objection, and he resolved it:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב המנונא, the one who asked the question in step 17.

phrases.english: It teaches separate cases:
'He made him swear about it': that is outside court,
and 'in court': that is where he jumped in and swore on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ, וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ; לִצְדָדִין קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 18 by splitting the משנה into two separate cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (לצדדין): the משנה describes two different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes one case where the שומר was made to swear in court, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's cases are 'made to swear outside court' and 'jumped in to swear in court.' Neither one is רב's case.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב from a ברייתא about a thief claim
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: a שומר claimed a thief stole the פקדון, swore, and then admitted, and witnesses came. If he admitted before the witnesses, he pays קרן וחומש and brings an אשם. If he admitted after the witnesses, he pays כפל and brings an אשם. So swearing did not exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: A homeowner who was holding a deposit claimed a thief stole it. He swore, then admitted, and witnesses came. If he admitted before the witnesses came, he pays the principal, a fifth, and brings a guilt offering. If he admitted after the witnesses came, he pays double and brings a guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new source, a ברייתא, to challenge רב's rule that a שומר who swore does not pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא the שומר swore, yet he still has to pay, either קרן וחומש or כפל. That looks like a direct contradiction of רב, who said swearing exempts him from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim that a thief stole the item
The value of the item plus an extra fifth
A guilt offering brought for a false oath
Double payment, the penalty for a thief

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁטָּעַן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב בְּפִקָּדוֹן
phrases.english: A homeowner who made the claim 'a thief took it' about a deposit
phrases.notes: The 'homeowner' here is the one who was holding the deposit, the שומר.

phrases.english: and he swore, and he admitted, and witnesses came:

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּאוּ עֵדִים הוֹדָה,
phrases.english: if he admitted before the witnesses came,
he pays the principal and a fifth, and brings a guilt offering;
and if he admitted after the witnesses came,
he pays double payment and brings a guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב המנונא's challenge was answered, רבא brings a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a שומר who swore about a פקדון does not pay.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has a שומר who swore and still pays קרן וחומש or כפל, so swearing did not exempt him.

steps.title: The earlier answers do not work for this ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that we cannot say this ברייתא is about an oath outside court or about a שומר who jumped in, because it says he pays כפל. כפל only applies to an oath he was made to take in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here you cannot say it is 'outside court' or 'he jumped in,' because the ברייתא teaches 'double payment'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes off the old escape routes, so רבא's challenge against רב stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רב was saved by saying the source was about an oath outside court or a שומר who jumped in. But כפל for a false thief claim only applies when the שומר was made to swear in court. So this ברייתא must be exactly רב's case, and it still makes him pay.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say
Double payment

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why the old answers no longer help. רבא will now have to limit רב's rule itself.

phrases.english: And here, 'outside court' and 'he jumped in'
you cannot say,
because it teaches 'double payment'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין וְקָפַץ לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes רבא's challenge stronger by blocking the 'outside court' and 'jumped in' answers that saved רב in steps 9, 12 and 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'outside court' or 'he jumped in' to defend רב against the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כפל only applies to an oath he was made to take in court, so the ברייתא must be about רב's own case.

steps.title: רבא limits רב's rule: it does not apply when he admits
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that whenever the שומר admits, whether he claimed the item was lost or claimed a thief took it, רב never said he is exempt. The פסוק 'והתודה' teaches that one who confesses must pay קרן וחומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Whenever he admitted, it makes no difference if he claimed it was lost and no difference if he claimed a thief took it. In these cases too, רב did not say his rule. For it is written 'and they shall confess,' which teaches that he must pay the principal and a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own challenge by making רב's rule smaller: it does not cover a שומר who admits on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule that the oath exempts him only applies when the שומר keeps denying. The ברייתא is about a שומר who admitted, and the תורה says plainly that a person who confesses pays קרן וחומש. So the ברייתא does not go against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He admitted
It makes no difference
The claim that the item was lost
'And they shall confess', the פסוק requiring payment after confession

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule that the oath exempts the שומר does not apply when he admits on his own, whether he claimed it was lost or claimed a thief took it. The פסוק 'והתודה' requires him to pay קרן וחומש.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Whenever he admitted,
it makes no difference if he claims it was lost,
and it makes no difference if he claims a thief took it,
in these cases too, Rav did not say his rule,
for it is written: 'And they shall confess',
which means he must pay the principal and a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from steps 20 and 21 by limiting how far רב's rule reaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule: רב's rule does not cover a שומר who admits.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule exempts every שומר who swore, even one who later admits.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the שומר admits, רב agrees he pays קרן וחומש, because of the פסוק 'והתודה'.

steps.title: Thief claim plus witnesses is also outside רב's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: if the שומר claimed a thief took it and witnesses came, רב also never said he is exempt, because the תורה writes כפל for that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, where he claims a thief took it and witnesses came, רב did not say his rule, because the תורה writes double payment for that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps narrowing רב's rule. After excluding a שומר who admits, he now excludes a שומר who claimed a thief took it and was then caught by witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה itself says that a שומר who falsely claims theft and is exposed pays כפל. רב could not have said such a שומר is exempt, because that would contradict a פסוק. So this case also falls outside רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim that a thief stole the deposit
Double payment
Witnesses

phrases.english: One who claims a thief took it
and witnesses came
also, רב did not say [his rule]
because double payment is written [in the Torah].

steps.triggerLanguage: טוען טענת גנב ובאו עדים נמי לא אמר רב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer from step 22 by excluding a second case from רב's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רב's rule frees even a שומר who claimed theft and was caught by witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: No. The Torah writes כפל for that case, so רב's rule cannot apply there.

steps.title: The exact case רב was talking about
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule only applies where the שומר claimed the item was lost, swore, did not admit, and then witnesses came.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he said it, it was where he claimed it was lost, swore, did not admit, and witnesses came.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives the one case where רב's rule does apply. It is a very narrow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he admitted nothing, there is no 'confession' to make him pay קרן וחומש. Because he claimed loss and not theft, the Torah's כפל does not apply. Only this case is left for רב's rule that the oath frees him.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim that the item was lost
And he swore
And he did not admit

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רב's rule covers only this case: a claim of loss, an oath, no admission, and then witnesses. Admitting brings in 'והתודה', and a claim of theft brings in כפל.

phrases.english: When he [רב] said it,
it was a case where he claims it was lost,
and swore, and did not admit,
and witnesses came.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי קאמר כגון שטוען טענת אבד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's limitation by naming the only case left for רב's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's rule that the oath frees the שומר applies only where he claimed loss, swore, never admitted, and was exposed by witnesses.

steps.title: רב אשי objects: רב המנונא knew רב's rule covered admitting
steps.stepSummary: רב גמדא repeats רבא's teaching to רב אשי. רב אשי objects: רב המנונא, רב's own student, challenged רב from a case of admitting, so he must have known the rule covered admitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גמדא went and said this teaching before רב אשי. He said to him: Now, רב המנונא was רב's student. He knew רב said his rule even where the שומר admitted, and so he challenged him from a case of admitting. And you say רב did not say it where he admitted?!
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a later generation. רב אשי hears רבא's limitation and attacks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said רב's rule never covered a שומר who admits. But רב המנונא, a direct student who would know his teacher's meaning, raised his question in step 17 from a משנה whose reason is that the swearer 'can go back and admit' and would then have to pay. That only works as a challenge if רב's rule covered admitting, so רבא's limitation seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
His student
He admitted
He challenges

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not attacking רב. He is attacking רבא's claim that רב's rule never applied to a שומר who admits.

phrases.english: רב גמדא went
and said this teaching before רב אשי.
phrases.notes: The teaching is רבא's limitation from steps 22 to 24.

phrases.english: He said to him: Now,
if רב המנונא, רב's student,
knew that רב said [his rule even where] he admitted,
and so challenged from [a case where] he admitted;
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from step 17. Its reason is that he can always go back and admit, and then he would have to pay.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ: הוֹדָה לָא אָמַר רַב?!
phrases.english: and you say רב did not say [it where] he admitted?!

steps.triggerLanguage: השתא ומה רב המנונא תלמידיה דרב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's limitation from steps 22 to 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רב's rule never applied to a שומר who admits
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own student challenged him from a case of admitting, which shows he knew the rule covered admitting. A student knows his teacher's meaning better than a later explanation does.

steps.title: רב אחא סבא begins to defend רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא סבא tells רב אשי that רב המנונא's real difficulty was something else, and starts to explain it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא סבא said to רב אשי: This is what was difficult for רב המנונא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב אחא סבא is about to explain what רב המנונא's question was really about. The explanation itself comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By reframing רב המנונא's question, רב אחא סבא will remove the proof that רב's rule covered admitting. This would let רבא's limitation stand.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא the Elder
Was difficult for him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא סָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: רב אחא the Elder said to רב אשי:

phrases.aramaic: רַב הַמְנוּנָא הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: This is what was difficult for רב המנונא:

steps.triggerLanguage: רב המנונא הכי קא קשיא ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering רב אשי's objection in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the earlier question (setup only; the content follows)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב המנונא's question proves that רב's rule covered a שומר who admitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב המנונא's difficulty was about something else, which is explained next.
